To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can recognize the board and the pieces on the board using the following method: 1) Detect the chess board by using a pre-defined chess board pattern and a chess board edge detector, 2) Segment the chess board into squares and recognize each chess piece by using an ensemble of classifiers trained on feature descriptor.

we have developed a method to recognize pieces on a chess board using classifiers trained on SIFT feature descriptors, that this method outperforms the state of the art, and that we have demonstrated its ability to be used in a real-time setting.
we present a novel method to segment chess boards and pieces using feature descriptors and a classifier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reconstructing a chess board from a given image.
the following problem: given a chess board, how can we automatically identify each piece and its location on the board?
the development of a robust and efficient method for recognizing chess pieces in images of chess boards.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented in this work is a significant improvement on existing methods in the field of board and piece recognition.
the proposed method for board and piece recognition is a robust and accurate approach that can be used to recognize a variety of chess boards and pieces in real-world settings.
this paper details a method of reconstructing a computer representation of a chess board from an image using board recognition and piece recognition techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to take an input image of a chessboard and reconstruct it as an image of the board with the pieces placed on the board.
we are able to take an image and output the board and pieces as an array of pieces.
we have created a robust system that recognizes chess pieces on a chess board and outputs the board and pieces as a computer representation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a robust piece recognition algorithm is possible using only a single RGB image of a chessboard.
we are able to achieve 100% accuracy in board recognition and 98% accuracy in piece recognition using only 10 training samples for each piece.
the use of feature descriptors and classifiers can greatly improve the performance and robustness of piece recognition algorithms.
